events.title: The September 11 attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks kill thousands of people in the United States. Communities mourn and help those affected.

events.title: Euro cash enters everyday use
events.description: Twelve countries introduce euro notes and coins.

events.title: Columbia is lost
events.description: The space shuttle breaks apart during its return to Earth, killing its seven crew members.

what_happened_next.text: Bonds led the seven choices. All three company shares lost heavily: Cisco lost more than three-quarters, while Microsoft and Amazon lost about half. The US basket also fell, but much less than those individual stocks. A useful technology and a promising business could still be disappointing investments at the price paid.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Investors saw online books, internet broadcasting and networking equipment as signs of a changing economy. Taiwan’s election and scientific discoveries competed for attention.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The price paid and the full five-year path mattered. Spreading money across many companies reduced dependence on these three badly hit shares.
reflection.what_faded_away: The number of people downloading a story did not reveal a software or networking company’s future return. Exciting new habits were not automatic stock-market gains.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: Nobody knew the size of the losses ahead. The internet’s importance did not make every share price reasonable or every company a winner.
